---
title: "Data Library"
---

This page is the book's running index of every raw dataset we use — where
each one came from, what we do with it, and where to grab it. You're
coding along without cloning the repo, so this is your one-stop shop for
pulling down the source data. It starts small and grows as the book
grows, so check back when a new chapter introduces a new file.

Every dataset lives in the top-level [`data/`
folder](https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/tree/main/data)
of the book's repository. For each file below you'll find its original
home on the [Connecticut Open Data Portal](https://data.ct.gov/) (the
"ODP") plus direct GitHub links — a **blob** link to browse it in the
browser and a **raw** link you can hand straight to `readr::read_csv()`
or download with your browser.

::: {.callout-note}
## These are snapshots

The files here are point-in-time snapshots, frozen so the book's code
gives everyone the same results. The live ODP datasets keep updating —
the APIs chapter shows you how to pull fresh data straight from the
source when you want it.
:::

## COVID-19 Tests, Cases, and Deaths by Town

**`ct-covid-by-town-2026-06-30.csv`** is the book's primary dataset — the
one the running analysis is built on. Each row is a Connecticut town's
cumulative COVID-19 tally (cases, deaths, tests, and rates) as of a given
report date, so the file is a stack of daily snapshots for all 169 towns.

- **What we use it for:** it drives the analysis from Chapter 1 through
  Chapter 4, including the maps in the data visualization chapter.
- **Coverage:** 169 CT towns, report dates spanning roughly
  **2020-03-24 to 2022-06-24**.
- **Snapshot taken:** 2026-06-30, from the ODP dataset **"COVID-19 Tests,
  Cases, and Deaths By Town — ARCHIVE"** (dataset id `28fr-iqnx`).

Links:

- ODP landing page: <https://data.ct.gov/Health-and-Human-Services/COVID-19-Tests-Cases-and-Deaths-By-Town-ARCHIVE/28fr-iqnx/about_data>
- SODA API endpoint (used in the APIs chapter): <https://data.ct.gov/resource/28fr-iqnx.json>
- GitHub (browse): <https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/blob/main/data/ct-covid-by-town-2026-06-30.csv>
- GitHub (raw download): <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/main/data/ct-covid-by-town-2026-06-30.csv>

## COVID-19 by Town — 2022 Excel demo slice

**`covid-2022.csv`** and **`covid-2022.xlsx`** are the same data in two
formats: a 2022-only slice of the COVID-by-town dataset above, carved out
purely to demonstrate reading Excel files with `readxl` in Further
Reading → [Working with Excel Files](../further-reading/excel-files.qmd).

Both files carry the same 16 columns as the primary dataset — `town`,
`total_cases`, `confirmed_cases`, `probable_cases`, `case_rate`,
`total_deaths`, `people_tested`, `number_of_tests`, and so on — cleaned
up to tidy `snake_case` names. The slice covers all 169 towns for report
dates from **2022-01-03 to 2022-06-24**.

Links:

- `covid-2022.csv` — [browse](https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/blob/main/data/covid-2022.csv) · [raw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/main/data/covid-2022.csv)
- `covid-2022.xlsx` — [browse](https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/blob/main/data/covid-2022.xlsx) · [raw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/main/data/covid-2022.xlsx)

## Synthetic COVID-19 line-list

::: {.callout-warning}
## This one is fake

**`synthetic-covid-linelist.csv` is not real data.** The town names and case
counts come from the real ODP dataset above, but every age, sex,
race/ethnicity, date, and outcome is randomly generated. No row is a real
person. It exists purely to practice case-level (one-row-per-case) work that
the aggregate files can't support. Never treat it as real DPH records.
:::

A synthetic line-list of ~35,000 COVID-19 cases in Hartford County during the
winter 2020–2021 surge — one row per case, with simulated demographics, onset
and report dates, hospitalization, and death. The [Building a
Dataset](../building-a-dataset/index.qmd) chapter walks through exactly how it
was made, and the generator that produced it is version-controlled at
[`data-raw/make-synthetic-linelist.R`](https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/blob/main/data-raw/make-synthetic-linelist.R)
(seeded, so it reproduces byte-for-byte).

- Based on ODP dataset `28fr-iqnx` (see above), scoped to Hartford County,
  Dec 2020 – Jan 2021.
- GitHub (browse): <https://github.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/blob/main/data/synthetic-covid-linelist.csv>
- GitHub (raw download): <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CT-DPH-Data-Management-and-Governance/modern-r-for-public-health-practitioners/main/data/synthetic-covid-linelist.csv>

## COVID-19 Cases and Deaths by Race and Ethnicity

Statewide COVID-19 cases and deaths broken out by race and ethnicity, from
the ODP dataset **"COVID-19 Cases and Deaths by Race/Ethnicity — ARCHIVE"**
(dataset id `7rne-efic`). It's earmarked here for future scenarios — a
demographic breakdown opens up questions the town-level file can't answer,
like disparities in outcomes across groups.

::: {.callout-note}
No local snapshot lives in `data/` yet. Once you download one and commit it
(same date-stamped convention as the other files), fill in its GitHub blob
and raw links here and update the "At a glance" row above.
:::

Links:

- ODP landing page: <https://data.ct.gov/Health-and-Human-Services/COVID-19-Cases-and-Deaths-by-Race-Ethnicity-ARCHIV/7rne-efic/about_data>
- SODA API endpoint: <https://data.ct.gov/resource/7rne-efic.json>
